history.summary: IDENTITY NOTE: several Laxmi Narayan temples exist in Faridabad (Sector 14, Sector 16, Gopi Colony-Old Faridabad/Deraval Sabha); no source carries the exact name 'Prachin Shri Laxmi Narayan Temple'. Documented here is the most prominent one: the Lakshmi Narayan Temple in Sector 14, managed by Narayan Seva Sansthan with Mahajan Sabha (Mahajan Biradari) Faridabad. Dr M. L. Gupta (1918-?, first qualified MBBS doctor of Faridabad, 1960) led the establishment of Mahajan Sabha Faridabad and the acquisition of land for this temple. The temple holds an annual foundation-day celebration (reported April 2026) and large Shri Krishna Janmashtami festivities jointly organised by Narayan Seva Sansthan and Mahajan Biradari. The 'Prachin' (ancient) claim is UNVERIFIED - no source dates the structure; if the CSV intended the Sector 16 or Gopi Colony shrine, this record needs correction.

town_description: Faridabad is the largest city of Haryana and a major industrial centre in the Delhi National Capital Region. Founded in 1607 by the Sufi saint Sheikh Farid Bukhari, after whom it is named, it grew from a Mughal-era settlement into an industrial township after Partition. Today it is one of India's biggest manufacturing hubs, with the Surajkund international crafts fair and several well-known temples in its sectors and old city.
